props.name: Misattribution

evidence.quote: assigning ECO2R performance to the catalyst’s initial morphology is misleading
the transformation begins at ECO2R onset, underscoring that the ″active″ structure is not defined solely by the as-prepared catalyst, but also by the onset environment of the reaction (Figure 3).

props.statement: Assigning ECO2R performance to the catalyst's initial morphology is misleading: the active structure is not defined solely by the as-prepared catalyst but also by the onset environment of the reaction, so structure−activity relationships that neglect dissolution−redeposition misattribute performance to the precursor.

props.name: Ocp activity

evidence.quote: Importantly, electrochemical measurements revealed that OCP-treated samples exhibited higher intrinsic activity (Figure 3). For a given applied current, these samples required a lower overpotential

props.scope: Cu foil samples with vs without OCP pretreatment, at −2, −5 and −10 mA applied current
props.statement: OCP-pretreated samples exhibited higher intrinsic activity: for a given applied current they required a lower overpotential, and operando EIS showed a substantially lower charge transfer resistance while the ECSA remained comparable, indicating that the specific activity of individual sites improved with OCP pretreatment.

props.name: Ocp selectivity

evidence.quote: GC data reveal that OCP pretreatment enhances ethylene and hydrogen selectivity while suppressing CO and methane formation.

props.scope: Cu foil, gas products, FEs normalized to 100 % (Figure 3)
props.statement: OCP pretreatment changes the ECO2R selectivity: it enhances ethylene and hydrogen selectivity while suppressing CO and methane formation (samples polarized immediately, without OCP, produced less hydrogen but also less ethylene, with improved selectivity toward CO and methane).

props.name: Oxidation state correlation

props.name: Reconstructed active surface

props.name: Universal mechanism

evidence.quote: we show that dissolution−redeposition is the universal early-stage restructuring mechanism in ECO2R, occurring across all the tested Cu morphologies, including foils, nanoparticles, oxide-derived films, and gas diffusion electrodes.

Our findings demonstrate that all the Cu catalysts act as precursors to their true, in situ-formed active phase, generated through the reduction of Cu oxides and electrolyte-driven dissolution-redeposition.

props.note: authors' conclusion from the IL-SEM/IL-STEM observations of Figures 1b, 2 and 3
props.scope: Cu-based ECO2R catalysts at the onset of the reaction
props.statement: Dissolution−redeposition is the universal early-stage restructuring mechanism in electrochemical CO2 reduction: it occurs across all the tested Cu morphologies (foils, nanoparticles, oxide-derived films, gas diffusion electrodes, carbon-coated nanowires), so Cu catalysts act as precursors to their true, in-situ-formed active phase.
